name: Skills.sh
summary: Vercel’s open directory and install leaderboard for agent skills.
description: Skills.sh ranks agent skills using installs reported by the open-source skills CLI. Browse the leaderboard or search for a skill, then open its listing to see the source repository, install command and supported agents.
bestFor: Discovering popular skills with quick CLI setup.
installGuide: Open a skill listing and copy its install command. To install a specific skill from a multi-skill repository, add --skill and the name from the listing.
pros: Install rankings help surface widely used skills.
The same CLI can target several coding agents.
cons: Install counts measure popularity.
Some skills rely on agent-specific tools.

name: AgenticSkills
summary: A handpicked directory organized by use case and coding agent.
description: AgenticSkills publishes an editorially selected catalog with category and platform filters. Skill pages include compatibility and install information. The site also covers MCP servers and workflows.
bestFor: Checking compatibility before choosing a skill.
installGuide: Open a listing, check the compatibility section for your agent, then follow the CLI or manual instructions on that page.
pros: A smaller catalog makes browsing more manageable.
Platform and category filters help narrow the options.
cons: Coverage is deliberately selective.
Available install methods vary by skill.

name: SkillsMP
summary: A searchable marketplace indexing public SKILL.md files from GitHub.
description: SkillsMP indexes public agent skills and links back to the repositories they came from. Search by task, skill name or GitHub account. Inspect the instructions and source before choosing an installation method.
bestFor: Finding niche skills across a large GitHub index.
installGuide: Open a search result, review the skill instructions, then follow the repository’s setup guide. Keep bundled scripts and resources with the SKILL.md file if you copy a folder manually.
pros: Useful for finding a skill by repository or creator.
Listings link to the underlying GitHub source.
cons: Quality and maintenance vary by repository.
Setup depends on the creator’s instructions.

name: SkillsMK
summary: Open-source agent skills grouped into 18 practical categories.
description: SkillsMK brings together SKILL.md-compatible projects from GitHub. Browse the catalog by category, filter by keyword, or check the leaderboard.
bestFor: Browsing an open-source catalog by technical topic.
installGuide: Open a listing and inspect its instructions. Follow the linked repository’s guide or put the complete skill folder in the location documented by your agent.
pros: Practical categories cover development, design and operations.
Skill listings identify the source repository.
cons: Compatibility depends on the individual skill.
Some projects require extra setup.

sources.label: Catalog, category count and skill count

name: DesignSkills.dev
summary: Design skills covering visual styles, UX patterns and motion.
description: DesignSkills.dev organizes practical design instructions around interface patterns, visual styles and the principles behind them. Each skill has a dedicated page with install instructions.
bestFor: Giving a coding agent a more specific design vocabulary.
installGuide: Open the skill you want and copy the install command provided on that skill’s page. Choose the agent you use if the installer prompts for a destination.
pros: Useful when you already know the design technique you want.
Skill pages turn design concepts into practical instructions.
cons: Coverage is focused on design and frontend work.
The listed platform set is smaller than general catalogs.

sources.label: Skill count, search and platform support

name: Awesome Agent Skills
summary: VoltAgent’s handpicked GitHub list of community and official skills.
description: VoltAgent maintains a directory of source repositories from engineering teams and independent contributors. Its README groups skills by publisher and topic and includes a compatibility table for major agents.
bestFor: Finding source repositories maintained by teams you recognize.
installGuide: Pick an entry from the README and open its source repository. Use that repository’s documented setup steps and check the agent paths in the compatibility table.
pros: Includes official vendor skills alongside independent projects.
Compatibility table covers installation paths across agents.
cons: The long README takes time to browse.
Individual repositories control updates and installation.

name: Anthropic Skills
summary: Anthropic’s official repository of example agent skills.
description: The Anthropic repository includes example skills, a starter template and reference implementations for document workflows. The README documents plugin installation in Claude Code and using skills in Claude.ai or through the API.
bestFor: Learning how to structure a skill from working examples.
installGuide: In Claude Code, register the marketplace, then open /plugin and choose the example-skills or document-skills plugin listed in the README.
pros: Examples show how SKILL.md works with bundled resources.
Official Claude Code installation instructions are available.
cons: Document reference implementations have separate license terms.
Some examples assume tools available in Claude.

name: Agent-Skills.md
summary: A searchable index of skill files with GitHub popularity signals.
description: Agent-Skills.md lists skills with short descriptions and GitHub activity figures. Open an entry to read more and locate its source before installing.
bestFor: Scanning GitHub skill listings by name and popularity.
installGuide: Find the entry, open its source, and follow the installation steps from that repository. For manual installs, use the complete skill folder and your agent’s documented path.
pros: Compact listings are quick to scan.
GitHub activity figures help identify active projects.
cons: Popularity and compatibility are separate considerations.
Some skills are written for a specific agent or operating system.

name: mdskills.ai
summary: A community directory for skills, plugins, MCP servers and rules.
description: mdskills.ai lists several kinds of agent resources together, with details and platform labels on individual listings. Browse by topic or search the skills catalog directly.
bestFor: Discovering skills alongside related plugins and MCP servers.
installGuide: Open a skill detail page and use its documented install command or download the skill. The site’s install guide lists locations for supported agents.
pros: Several agent resource types are searchable from one place.
Listings expose compatibility and setup information.
cons: The advertised total includes plugins and MCP servers.
Check which type of resource you are opening.

name: Claude Marketplaces
summary: A catalog of Claude Code plugins, skills and marketplace sources.
description: Claude Marketplaces surfaces third-party Claude Code plugin listings and their source marketplaces. It helps you find bundles of skills and related tools and identify which marketplace to add in Claude Code.
bestFor: Finding skills distributed as Claude Code plugins.
installGuide: Open a plugin listing and confirm the source marketplace in its instructions. Add that marketplace in Claude Code, then use /plugin to select and install the plugin.
pros: Plugin and marketplace source information is in one place.
Listings expose bundles that contain multiple skills.
cons: Installation is specific to Claude Code.
A plugin may also include hooks, servers or other components.
